sentences.text: Tarbosaurus is a genus containing the single recognized species Tarbosaurus bataar, a large tyrannosaurid dinosaur.
The largest individuals measured between 10 and 12 meters in length and weighed up to 4.5 to 5 metric tons.
This predator possessed approximately sixty large teeth and a unique jaw locking mechanism.
A joint Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered a large theropod skull and vertebrae in the Nemegt Formation in 1946.
In 1955, Evgeny Maleev designated specimen PIN 551-1 as the holotype for the species Tyrannosaurus bataar, though the specific name 'bataar' is a misspelling of the Mongolian word for 'hero'.
Tarbosaurus was an apex predator that preyed on ankylosaurids like Tarchia and Saichania, as well as sauropods including Nemegtosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia.
A juvenile individual found was estimated to be 2 to 3 years old when it died, and examination of sclerotic rings suggests it may have been a crepuscular or nocturnal hunter.
Tarbosaurus belongs to the theropod subfamily Tyrannosaurinae within the family Tyrannosauridae.
Some experts consider Tarbosaurus to be synonymous with the North American genus Tyrannosaurus, and some researchers have supported classifying Tarbosaurus bataar as a species of Tyrannosaurus.
It was previously thought that Alioramus was the closest relative of Tarbosaurus, but this hypothesis has been disproven.
Tarbosaurus bataar is known from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia, and fragmentary remains have been found in the Subashi Formation of China.
The dinosaur lived in a humid floodplain environment containing deserts, forests, plains, and river channels, specifically a wet alluvial terrain cut by river channels.
Some scholars suspect that a second species of Tarbosaurus may exist.

Dong and Currie suggested that Shanshanosaurus might be a juvenile Tarbosaurus, though they did not formally assign it to the genus, while Currie speculated that Alioramus might be a juvenile Tarbosaurus but noted features like tooth count and snout crests suggested otherwise.
It is debated whether tyrannosaurid remains found in the Djadokhta Formation belong to Tarbosaurus, with some researchers listing them as a dubious species.
